[Testo](https://github.com/php-testo/testo) plugins for code that uses Thesis packages.

## Installation

```shell
composer require --dev thesis/testo-plugin
```

Requires 64-bit PHP 8.6+.

## The event loop

A wait of [thesis/async](https://github.com/thesis-php/async) outside a run of its event loop throws
`LogicException`. `EventLoopPlugin` and the `#[EventLoop]` attribute run a test as the body of a `Thesis\Async\group()`,
on the real clock, so the test itself can wait. The real-time and virtual-time attributes use the same setup
described below.

## Virtual time

`VirtualTimePlugin` and the `#[VirtualTime]` attribute run a test in its own `Thesis\Async\virtualTime()`
of [thesis/async](https://github.com/thesis-php/async): the clock jumps to the next timer whenever nothing can run,
so `delay(hours(1))` is over at once and durations can be asserted exactly. How the virtual clock behaves is described
in the README of thesis/async.

Fibers ready in the same tick run in a shuffled order. Each test gets a random seed. A test that
counts on one order fails sooner or later, as it would on a loaded machine. A test that fails prints its seed,
and `THESIS_SEED` replays it:

```
Seed 2242033608576963125: replay with THESIS_SEED=2242033608576963125.
```

Every test of a suite, with the plugin in `testo.php`:

```php
use Testo\Application\Config\ApplicationConfig;
use Testo\Application\Config\SuiteConfig;
use Thesis\TestoPlugin\VirtualTimePlugin;

return new ApplicationConfig(
    suites: [
        new SuiteConfig(name: 'unit', location: [__DIR__ . '/tests'], plugins: [new VirtualTimePlugin()]),
    ],
);
```

Or only some, with the attribute on a test class or a test:

```php
use Testo\Assert;
use Testo\Test;
use Thesis\Async\Instant;
use Thesis\TestoPlugin\VirtualTime;
use function Thesis\Async\delay;
use function Thesis\Time\hours;

#[Test]
final class HeartbeatTest
{
    #[VirtualTime]
    public function waitsAnHour(): void
    {
        $start = Instant::now();

        delay(hours(1));

        Assert::equals(Instant::now()->since($start), hours(1));
    }
}
```

The lifecycle hooks of a test (`#[BeforeTest]`, `#[AfterTest]`) run on its clock, and every data set gets a clock
of its own. A test that has the attribute in a suite with the plugin is not wrapped twice.

## PHP errors

PHP only prints a warning, a notice or a deprecation, and the test passes. `PhpErrorsPlugin` throws one
as `ErrorException` where it happens, in the test and in the tasks it starts alike, so the test fails
and the trace points at the cause. An error suppressed by `@` is left alone, and a handler that the test sets itself
sees the errors first.

Every suite, with the plugin in `testo.php`:

```php
use Testo\Application\Config\ApplicationConfig;
use Testo\Application\Config\SuiteConfig;
use Thesis\TestoPlugin\PhpErrorsPlugin;

return new ApplicationConfig(
    suites: [
        new SuiteConfig(name: 'unit', location: [__DIR__ . '/tests']),
    ],
    plugins: [new PhpErrorsPlugin()],
);
```
